item.title: iPhone zooms in when tapping form inputs, and wide table overflows on tablet
item.dc:creator: member6
item.description:
Replies: 0

Hi,

I have two mobile/tablet layout problems on my homepage and I’m not sure if they come from the theme styles or my own content.

1) Input zoom on iPhone
The first text input in the calculator form on the homepage has a computed font size of about 14.7px. On iPhone, Safari zooms the page in when you tap it, and the user has to pinch back out. The other inputs/selects are 20px or more and don’t cause this. Where does Kadence set the base font size for form inputs, and what’s the cleanest way to make all inputs at least 16px on mobile?

2) Table overflow on tablet (768px)
The tax bracket tables are fine on a phone (they shrink to about 310px), but at a 768px wide viewport one table renders around 957px wide and runs off the screen. Is there a Kadence option to make tables scroll horizontally inside their container, or should I wrap them myself?

Desktop looks fine in both cases.

Thanks for any pointers!

item.title: Full-width (alignfull) group blocks cause horizontal scroll on mobile
item.dc:creator: member6
item.description:
Replies: 0

Hi,

On my homepage, the sections I built with Group blocks set to Full width (alignfull) are slightly wider than the screen on mobile, so the whole page can be dragged sideways a little.

What I see at a 360px wide viewport:
– the visible width is about 338px, but the alignfull groups render at about 361px
– they get a negative left margin of around -37px and 20px left/right padding
– the page scroll width becomes about 358px, so there is roughly 20px of horizontal scroll
– the same thing happens at 768px (tablet), with about 20px extra

It looks fine on desktop. Normal-width blocks are fine; only the full-width groups overflow.

Is this a known issue with Astra’s full-width alignment on mobile, or is there a setting (container layout / content width) I should change? I’d prefer a proper fix over just adding overflow-x: hidden to the body.

Thanks!

item.title: Sitemap: category lastmod is 1970-01-01; index lastmod counts scheduled posts
item.dc:creator: member2
item.description:
Replies: 0

AIOSEO version: 5.0.4 (Lite, latest on wordpress.org)

WordPress version: 7.1.4

Theme: Zeever (block theme)

Example URLs: https://member2.com/category-sitemap.xml and https://member2.com/sitemap.xml

Hello AIOSEO team,

I found two problems with sitemap <lastmod> values while auditing our site. I read the 5.0.4 source and I think I’ve found the cause of both. Details are below.

Bug 1: Category sitemap <lastmod> is 1970-01-01 for categories with no child categories

What happens

In category-sitemap.xml, every category that has published posts but no child categories shows:

<lastmod><![CDATA[1970-01-01T00:00:00+00:00]]></lastmod>

A parent category shows the date of its child category’s newest post, not its own. On our site, “Car Review” shows 2026-10-18 even though its own posts were updated later. That date comes from its child category “For Sale”.

Cause (as far as I can tell)

• app/Common/Sitemap/Content.php, terms() (line ~386) gets terms through aioseo()->sitemap->query->terms(). It then calls getTermLastModified( $term ) for each entry (line 411).

• app/Common/Sitemap/Query.php, terms() (line 366) selects only t.term_id by default (line 368). tt.count is added only when the root argument is set (line 380). So for the normal, non-root sitemap build, the term objects have no count property.

• app/Common/Sitemap/Content.php, getTermLastModified() (line 431) checks if ( empty( $term->count ) ) (line 442). Because count is never set, this is always true, so it always runs the “parent term with no posts” branch. That branch takes MAX(post_modified_gmt) only over posts in terms whose parent equals this term.

• A category with no children gets NULL back. dateTimeToIso8601( '' ) then turns that into 1970-01-01. A category with children gets only its children’s newest date.

Steps to reproduce

1. Install AIOSEO 5.0.4 with sitemaps on and the Category taxonomy included.

2. Create a category with no child categories and assign one published post to it.

3. Open /category-sitemap.xml.

Expected: <lastmod> equals the newest post_modified_gmt of the published posts in that category.

Actual: <lastmod> is 1970-01-01T00:00:00+00:00. A parent category shows only its children’s newest date.

Possible fix

Select tt.count in Query::terms() for the regular build too, or don’t rely on $term->count in getTermLastModified() (for example, call get_term() when count isn’t set). Also, when no date is found, leave <lastmod> out rather than outputting the epoch.

Bug 2: Sitemap index <lastmod> for taxonomy sitemaps counts unpublished/scheduled posts (shows a future date)

What happens

In sitemap.xml, the category-sitemap.xml entry shows a future date:

<loc>https://member2.com/category-sitemap.xml</loc>

<lastmod>2026-11-19T16:35:00+00:00</lastmod>

(This was checked on 2026-10-31 UTC.) The date matches a scheduled post (status future, publishing 2026-11-19 16:35 UTC) in one of our categories.

Cause (as far as I can tell)

• app/Common/Sitemap/Root.php, buildIndexes() (line 532), taxonomy branch (around lines 566–591). It runs MAX(p.post_modified_gmt) over every post in the chunk’s terms (WHERE tt.term_id IN (...), line 584) but has no post_status = 'publish' condition. So drafts, private posts and scheduled (future) posts count too, and a scheduled post’s future date ends up as the index lastmod.

• The post-type branch of the same function (line 555, whereIn( 'p.ID', $ids )) uses IDs from the sitemap query, so it isn’t affected in the same way.

• getTermLastModified() in Content.php does filter p.post_status = 'publish', so the two code paths disagree.

Steps to reproduce

1. Include the Category taxonomy in the sitemap.

2. Schedule a post for a future date in any included category.

3. Open /sitemap.xml.

Expected: The category-sitemap.xml lastmod reflects only published posts, and is never later than the current time.

Actual: It shows the scheduled post’s future date.

Possible fix

Add ->where( 'p.post_status', 'publish' ) (and, if you like, limit it to the included post types) to the taxonomy lastmod query in Root::buildIndexes().

Environment notes

• Sitemap settings: indexes on, 1000 links per index, post types post/page/attachment, taxonomy category only, author and date sitemaps off.

Thank you for looking into this. I’m happy to give more details or test a fix.

item.title: AI Engine 3.8.8 Free: supported way to use store=false with the Responses API?
item.dc:creator: member1
item.description:
Replies: 1

Hello Jordy,

I’m using AI Engine 3.8.8 Free with OpenAI’s Responses API. I found your reply in the “AI Engine – Chatbot privacy and data retention questions” thread. I understand from it that AI Engine does not currently send store: false and that the Automatic history strategy relies on the previous response. Could you please confirm whether this applies to version 3.8.8 Free?

  1. Is there a built-in setting in AI Engine 3.8.8 Free to send store: false with every Responses API request?
  2. If not, is there a documented filter, action hook, or other supported, update-safe way to add this parameter without modifying the plugin’s core files?
  3. If store: false is used, can conversation context continue across messages? If so, which history strategy is supported?
  4. If the Free version has no supported way to do this, what approach do you recommend for users who need store: false while preserving conversation continuity?

Thank you.
